title: Parallel reduction
description: Counts primes below 2,000,000 by trial division (odd divisors up to the square root). Numbers are dealt out to 4 workers in an interleaved pattern (worker t takes n where n mod 4 = t) and the partial counts are summed.
pseudocode:
isPrime(n) = n >= 2 and no odd divisor d <= sqrt(n) divides n   (n = 2 is prime, even n > 2 is not)

worker(t):                               # t = 0..3
    count = 0
    for n = t; n < 2,000,000; n += 4:
        if isPrime(n): count++
    return count

start 4 workers (threads / processes) running worker(0..3)
print sum of their counts
reveals: Thread creation, scheduling and scaling on a 4-core runner.
caveat: Thread count, scheduling and synchronisation matter. Python uses multiprocessing (processes) because of the GIL; Node uses worker_threads; Ruby and PHP also use separate processes. GitHub-hosted runners have 4 vCPUs (public repos) which are hyper-threads.
